predecessors.name: Islamic state of Medina
predecessors.text: Medina and the Hejaz, then Arabia re-united in the Ridda wars (633)

successors.name: Umayyad Caliphate
successors.text: the whole caliphate, to which Mu'awiya succeeded in 661

ledger.x: 632: Abu Bakr succeeds Muhammad at Medina as the first caliph.
632: the Ridda wars begin.
633: Khalid's Iraq campaign.
633: Arabia is re-united.
633: the Ridda wars end with Arabia re-united (18 March 633).

633: Khalid took Ullais 'in May' and 'attacked the city of Hira in the last week of the month' (infobox 'May 633'); 'The inhabitants paid a large tribute to spare the city', so Hira pays tribute rather than being annexed.
634: the first campaigns into Syria and Palestine.
634: Damascus falls on 19 September 634 (Rashidun page); the Levant page says 'Damascus capitulated in sometime of August or September 635'.
Year not on the pages for the wider southern Iraq: Hira is now its own event (May 633, Battle of Hira page), but the page is silent on Ubulla, Anbar and Ayn al-Tamr.
634: the Ghassanids.
Year not on the page: the infobox lists the Ghassanids among the states preceding the caliphate and the Levant page is silent on their fate after the invasion (Jabala was their last king).

Year not on the page: the contest with the Ghassanids ends when the whole of Syria falls after the Yarmuk (August 636, Rashidun page); the Levant page says nothing of the Ghassanids after the first campaign.
636: the Yarmuk.
637: Ctesiphon falls.
637: the fighting for the Sawad ends with Ctesiphon in March 637; by February 638 'the Suwad and the Tigris and Euphrates valleys were under full Muslim control'.
637: 'Jerusalem surrendered in April 637.'
637: 'Antioch surrendered on 30 October 637.'
637: the main war for Syria ends with Antioch (30 October 637); the coast of Palestine holds out to 639-641.
Late 638: Ahvaz.
638: Hulwan 'was captured in January 638' and 'By February 638, the Suwad and the Tigris and Euphrates valleys were under full Muslim control'.
638-639: 'Byzantine Armenia was conquered in 638-639' (Persia page).
639: 'In December 639, Amr ibn al-As left for Egypt with a force of 4,000 troops.'
639-640: 'In August 639 Iyad marched on Raqqa'; its capture is dated 639 or 640 and between late 639 and December 640 his forces 'subdued a series of cities'.
639-641: 'Caesarea and Ascalon ... surrendered between 639 and 641'; 640 is the middle of the range.
Year not on the page: Hormuzan 'later broke' the late-638 treaty; 'Persian reinforcements arrived in late 640', so 640 is my bridging.
Late 640: Persian reinforcements arrive and the Battle of Tustar follows (the page gives no month for Tustar).
641: Susa was 'captured in January 641 after a siege of a couple of months'; Junde Sabur surrendered after a siege of a few weeks (undated).
641: the Khuzestan campaign ends with Susa in January 641.
642: 'In the summer of 642, 'Amr ibn al-'As sent an expedition to the Christian kingdom of Nubia.'
642: 'The first Arab invasion began in 642 with the capture of the strategically important city of Derbent.'
642: Egypt is Muslim.
642: the Egyptian campaign ends with the end of the armistice on 29 September.
642: the Persians were defeated 'at the Battle of Nahavand in December 642'; the Hamadan district fell after it with weak resistance (it rebelled and was retaken in 651).

Year not on the page: the page never dates Rey's first submission, but says 'Hamadan and Rey had rebelled' and, in the Khorasan paragraph, 'Rey was already in Muslim hands', so Rey was under Muslim authority before 651.
Year not on the page: Isfahan was taken after Nahavand and the siege lasted 'a few months', with conflicting commander accounts and no surrender date.
643: 'Suhail ibn Adi marched from Basra in 643 and subdued the province after a pitched battle.'

642/643: 'Soon after the fall of Alexandria in 642, Amr ibn al-As continued westwards into Cyrenaica and Tripolitania'; 'Barqa fell without opposition, treaties were made with the Luwata Berbers exacting a tribute of 13,000 dinars'.
643: 'Tripoli was more difficult, its garrison being supported by the Christian Berber tribes of Nafusa, but after around a month it also fell in around 643.'
644: expeditions reached Tiflis in late 643 and 'By Umar's death in November 644, almost the whole of the South Caucasus' was captured.

644: 'In late 644 CE Caliph Umar dispatched an army under the command of Hakam ibn Amr for the wholesale invasion of Makran' (a raid in 643); 'In mid-644 the Battle of Rasil was fought' against the Rai dynasty, and Umar ordered that Makran 'should be the easternmost frontier'.

End of 645: 'Constans sent a large fleet of 300 ships to retake Egypt towards the end of 645'; Manuel's troops 'landed without resistance and easily overpowered small Arab garrison at Alexandria' (about 1000 Arab soldiers).
646: 'The main rebellions were in the Persian provinces of Armenia and Azerbaijan in 646' (Persia page).
646: Amr, sent by Uthman, beat the Byzantines at the Battle of Nikiou, who 'retreated in disarray, back to Alexandria'; 'the Arabs managed to batter the walls down and storm the city'.
646: the same sentence names Azerbaijan; 'The conquest of Iranian Azerbaijan started in 651', so the revolt runs to 651.
647: Sufetula.
Year not on the page: 'Muslim forces later withdrew to Barqa'.
648: 'Istakhr surrendered in 648.'
649: 'Mu'awiya's navy took Cyprus in 649, and Crete and Rhodes followed.'
649: the rebellions list has 'Fars and Sistan in 649'; Istakhr's citizens 'rebelled in 649/650'.
Year not on the page: 'Meanwhile, Hamadan and Rey had rebelled' is undated and sits in the 651 paragraph, so 650 is my bridging; the reconquest is 651.
650: the rebellions list reads 'Fars and Sistan in 649, Makran in 650, and Khorasan in 651'.
651: 'Ahnaf ibn Qais took Nishapur without resistance', Herat fell after a siege of a few months and Merv was 'occupied without a fight'; Yazdegerd III was killed near Merv in 651.
651: 'Rabi ibn Ziyad took Zaranj, and its governor Aparviz agreed to a tribute of 1 million dirhams'; Sistan had rebelled in 649 and Mujashi's 650 invasion was beaten.

651: 'Nu'aym recaptured Hamadan after a bloody battle, and then proceeded to Rey'; Rey was 'besieged' and 'surrendered after fierce resistance', the Persians 'were defeated outside the fort, and the Muslims recaptured the city'.

651: the Azerbaijan reconquest 'started in 651' (Hudhayfah took Zanjan, Ardabil 'which surrendered peacefully' and Bab al-Abwab 'by force'); the page also has Azerbaijan surrendering to Umar, who died in 644, which it does not reconcile.

650/651: Istakhr 'was soon sacked by the Arabs, who killed over 40,000 defenders' and they 'quickly seized Gor, Kazerun and Siraf'; 'Muslim control of Fars remained shaky for a time, with several local rebellions following'.
Outcome not on the page: Makran is only named in 651 as 'part of a simultaneous attack launched against Kerman and Makran in the southeast'.
651: Hudhayfah's march ends the Azerbaijani revolt that began in 646.
652: Balanjar.
651-2: 'A treaty was finally concluded with the Nubians in 651-2'; the Rashidun page calls it a non-aggression treaty after Uthman's governor sent another army 'ten years later'.
653: 'Rshtuni voluntarily agreed to submit to Muslim overlordship' when Constans' truce with the Arabs ended in 653; the page gives no 652/653 treaty date beyond that.
653: Armenia submits under Rshtuni and stays a tributary; the page has Rshtuni evicting Byzantine garrisons in 654 and invaded Byzantine Armenia in 655; he died at Damascus in 656.
656: the capital moves from Medina to Kufa (infobox: 'Medina (632-656); Kufa (656-661)').

656: Uthman is killed 'in June 656' and Ali's accession 'triggered the First Fitna'; Mu'awiya, long governor of the Levant, holds Syria against Ali (the Rashidun page: Ali's forces 'lost control over most of the caliphate's territory to Mu'awiya').
Dec 656: 'Rebels captured Basra from Ali's governor'; 'The two parties fought the Battle of the Camel in December 656' and Ali won; fighting there began on 8 December.
Dec 656: Ali wins the Battle of the Camel and holds Basra.
657: 'with the outbreak of the First Muslim Civil War in 657, effective Arab authority in the country ceased'; Mamikonian 'returned to Byzantine overlordship almost immediately'.
657: the Armenian princes return to Byzantine overlordship (mirror of byzantine-empire /ledger/20, which cites the same page).
657: Siffin. 'Fighting began on Wednesday, 26 July' and an arbitration agreement followed on 2 August 657; a stalemate. The page I read does not place the battlefield.

658: 'In mid-658, Mu'awiya I intervened directly in Egypt'; Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr (who replaced Qays ibn Sa'd in 657) was executed and Amr ibn al-As reinstated: 'the Umayyad annexation of Egypt took place in 658'.
660: 'In 660, Busr then continued his expedition into Yemen'; Ali held the Hejaz and Yemen until Busr's raids, and Jariya later restored his authority in Yemen.
Late 660: letters between Ali and Mu'awiya: 'both parties agreed to cease military campaigns'; the offer that Ali keep Iraq and Mu'awiya Syria.
661: Hasan cedes the caliphate and the contest ends.
661: 'In January 661, while praying at the Great Mosque of Kufa', Ali was killed; Hasan, proclaimed at Kufa, 'concluded a peace treaty with Mu'awiya', ceding the caliphate after six months.
661: the Rashidun Caliphate ends.

wars.name: Ridda wars
wars.outcome: Medina's victory: the peninsula 'united under the caliph in Medina' by 18 March 633.

wars.name: Muslim conquest of Persia
wars.outcome: Muslim victory: 'Annexation of the Sasanian Empire by the Rashidun Caliphate'; Yazdegerd III killed near Merv in 651.

wars.name: Muslim conquest of the Levant
wars.outcome: Muslim victory: 'Annexation of Byzantine Syria by the Rashidun Caliphate' (infobox 634-638); Damascus 634/5, Yarmuk August 636, Jerusalem April 637, Antioch October 637.

wars.name: Muslim conquest of Egypt
wars.outcome: Muslim victory: Egypt 'under Arab rule within two years'; the Byzantines briefly retook Alexandria at the end of 645 and Amr retook it in 646.

wars.name: Arab-Khazar wars (first war)
wars.outcome: Khazar victory at Balanjar in 652: the first Arab invasion began in 642 with Derbent and ended in a decisive Arab defeat.

wars.name: First Fitna
wars.outcome: Umayyad victory: Ali killed January 661, Hasan abdicated, 'Establishment of the Umayyad Caliphate'.

certainty.note: Desert and steppe frontiers and conquest-era control; no treaty line.
